newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Jan-April steel output up vs '96 - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Jan-April steel output up vs '96 - agency.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Smederevo and Niksic iron and steel works produced 314,156 tonnes of crude steel in January-April, 228,407 tonnes more than in the same period last year, state news agency Tanjug reported on Friday.

The Smederevo works produced 281,741 tonnes of steel, or 230,603 tonnes more than in the same period 1996, while Niksic output dropped by 2,196 tonnes to 32,415 tonnes compared to last year's figure, the agency quoted the Yugoslav Iron and Steel Federation as saying in a report.

After continuous growth in the first three months of the year, total crude steel output in April dropped by 7,467 tonnes compared to March, with Smederevo output down 6,445 and Niksic 1,019 tonnes on the previous month.
Problems in securing domestic and imported raw materials and fuels, difficulties in marketing products and insolvency are seen as the main reasons April output was below plan.

The situation on the local market is still being complicated by imports of steel at dumping prices, especially from eastern European countries, and producers are calling for higher customs tariffs for imports of that steel which is already produced in the country.

According to the report, the country's two iron and steel mills and metal processing companies produced a total of 297,097 tonnes of finished steel products in the January-April period, or 178,051 tonnes more than the same period last year.
Due to reduced domestic demand, the bulk of finished products, some 69 percent, is earmarked for export, the report said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
